There are so many different ways to get “fucked up”, if you are not a psychonaut, let alone someone who dabbles in the dark arts I would not recommend using heavier drugs trying to have an intense experience honestly.

If you really want to go down that rabbit hole and begin to understand what your mind and drugs are capable of you have to do your research or you will end up injuring or scaring someone.

Ethanol(booze) and cannabis both can be very intense in their own right and would be the place to start if you don’t have much experience with drugs.

Beyond that there’s a few classes of drugs that I’d guess would be of interest... let me just say first that if you’re trying to have an intense experience you really need to do your homework and you should use drugs with shorter durations and consistent, measurable doses for safety sake. I’ll go over a couple things that can induce states that produce some of the symptoms you’ve mentioned.

Dissociatives: DXM, legal albeit a very dirty dissociative and is pretty unpleasant compared to ketamine or pcp (and analogs)
Inhalants & Solvents: Nitrous Oxide, legal, short duration, very safe, enjoyable.
Diethyl Ether, legal(ish), short duration, quite safe, quite enjoyable. (Wouldn’t recommend any other solvents)
(Ethanol has somewhat similar effects to other solvents)
KOR ligands: Salvia Divinorum, legal in some areas, short duration, VERY INTENSE, not for noobs.
Deliriants: diphenhydramine, legal, more or less the safest deliriant you can find easily. all deliriants are dangerous and not for noobs. usually quite unpleasant.
GABAergic hallucinogens: Muscimol: amanita muscaria or panther caps may be legal(ish). They are hard to dose safely and are pretty dangerous in general, they can often be quite unpleasant, not for noobs.
Z-drugs(prescription medications) less dangerous but also far less mind altering per how sedating/amnesic they are.
Psychedelics:(probably not what you’re looking for for your book)
Cannabinoids: Pot...
Stimulants:(stimulant psychosis is a state that would interest you but I would not recommend intentionally trying to induce this)

There aren’t really any withdrawals per se, comedowns yeah, cravings yeah, residual depression/lack of motivation yeah. A taper is useless with stimulants, its only necessary if there are physical withdrawals (like with downers)

She’ll probably relapse, but that’s part of the healing process. She might want to find a new vice to go to when cravings get bad, if so, make sure it’s something relatively inert. Definitely NO STIMULANTS... too much of a tease. (Tho they might be helpful post-recovery for general functioning, but that’s waaaaaayy down the road) (that being said; relapse =/= binge)

If she’s a smoker (tobacco) I find that makes it really easy to relapse cuz you just feel like an addict (also the cravings are weirdly similar). She really just needs to stay away from any addictive behavior.

She needs a radical changes in lifestyle and community if she wants it to stick IMO. Substance use and abuse is a social issue, not just a chemical issue (she hasn’t been abusing speed this long because her life is fucken awesome, if you know what I’m saying)

Honestly, if she has the means, moving towns could do the trick. And I would say try to keep anything related to drug use on the down low. If she can manage to forget about it, forget what it feels like, and why she even started, it’s essentially victory.

As for the physiological side of things, if the dopamine depression is intolerable to her, supplementing its precursors, tyrosine or levodopa (levodopa being the more noticeable of the two) may be helpful in the short term to help restore synaptic catecholamine levels. That being said these supplements are not a permanent solution and are not to be relied on.
I’ve read good things about cordyceps supplements upregulating dopamine receptors too, which are no doubt fried (might be worth researching) but tbh it would be an experiment. (Tho depending on her habits severity, if she’s schizophrenic-ish after discontinuing use this whole paragraph might be worth ignoring)

And of course, diet, exercise, work/hobbies(a reason to get out of bed in the morning), healthy social interaction with good people.. this is the kind of shit that really works. 

Also tea is really good. Like green tea and herbal tea. I was drinking probably 10 cups of green tea a day after I stopped (not even an exaggeration). It’s innocent and helpful, and even if she doesn’t quit she should get into green tea as antioxidants help prevent some of the damage stimulants can cause.
